meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as read side by side for Proof Reader (wcook04/proof-reader 3858afbe00b2, papers/navier-stokes-library-15). Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted or AI-assessed; no mathematician has reviewed them.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).

notes.Breakdown.FracNoBoundedSolution: The obstruction quantifies over a single energy bound uniform for all nonnegative times; it does not rule out a competitor merely because its energy is finite at each separate time.
notes.Breakdown.Freq.fracBilinX: This operator is chosen from its bilinear specification when the required branch exists and has a zero fallback; existence and formula theorems establish the intended positive time branch.
notes.Breakdown.Freq.fracDilX: The dilation definition returns zero outside positive scales; its algebraic scaling laws are stated under positive scale assumptions.
notes.Breakdown.Freq.fracHeatFactor: The heat factor uses time clamped at zero, so its nonpositive time branch is part of the definition.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.FracGlueUnbounded: This proposition is parameterized by α without building α > 1 into the definition; its supplying theorem uses that assumption to obtain a positive dilation exponent.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.FracTorusDrift: The drift construction preserves the original initial datum; the contract does not impose a zero mean normalization on that datum.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.fracSourceOp: This source operator is selected from its continuous linear map specification and has a zero fallback; positive scale existence results are needed to identify its intended action.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.fracTorusForce: This choice based forcing definition has a zero fallback when its specification is not realized; a separate existence theorem identifies the Fourier realization.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.fracTorusHeat: This choice based definition has a zero fallback when the requested operator specification is not realized; the torus heat existence theorem supplies its intended realization.
notes.Breakdown.Periodic.fracTorusKernel: This choice based definition has a zero fallback when the requested kernel specification is not realized; the torus kernel existence theorem supplies its intended realization in its stated exponent range.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.PowerMildBoundState: No named provider or explicit caller was located in the supplied library. The nearby mild-flow exports have different statements.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.PowerMildSubStateme: No named provider or explicit caller was located in the supplied library. The nearby mild-flow exports have different statements.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.PowerMildUniqueStat: No named provider or explicit caller was located in the supplied library. The nearby mild-flow exports have different statements.
notes.Breakdown.SmoothFlow.powerHeatSymbol: This symbol uses the actual time parameter without clamping it at zero; nonnegative time assumptions are therefore material in contraction estimates.
